Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

We are meeting Sunday at eight thirty in the morning beside the blue kayak rack at the north end of the public lot. The forecast in the harbor notice says cloudy with a chance of showers after noon, so bring a light rain jacket, but we are still planning to meet unless the town closes the beach. I checked with the parks desk yesterday, and they said the lot gate will be open by eight, though the restrooms may not be unlocked until nine.

We have about twenty-six people signed up so far, including six students from Harborview High and three people from the kayak club. Please bring your own work gloves if you have them, and wear shoes that can get wet, not sandals. I have extra gloves in two sizes and a few pairs of rubber boots, but not enough for everyone. The club is bringing four grabbers, and the town will leave a bundle of orange bags near the rack. I asked for the smaller bags too because they are easier to tie when the wind picks up, and we should keep the bags out of the dune grass while we work.

We are not taking driftwood or shells, and we should leave the seaweed where it is unless there is plastic tangled in it. If you find a bird that seems injured, keep people back and call me rather than trying to handle it. Luis has the number for the wildlife office saved on his phone, but I will also have it on the paper contact sheet. One of the new volunteers asked whether we could move the broken cooler near the creek, and I told her, “Let’s look at it together first.” It may have a sharp edge, so please let me check before anybody touches it.

For lunch, I am bringing coffee, oranges, and a box of granola bars. Maya, could you bring drinking water if you still have the two refill jugs from the school event? If not, just let me know and I will ask the kayak club. We will set everything on the folding table near the rack, not on the low wall by the dunes. There is a tap beside the public restrooms, but last time the handle was stiff and the water ran slowly. We can use it to rinse muddy gloves if it is working, but please do not count on it for drinking water.

About the weigh-in, we have the hanging scale from the community shed and a spare battery in the side pocket. Last time I said we could weigh every bag, but that slowed the pickup down, so this time we will weigh the full bags at the end of each section instead. Please keep bags that contain glass separate from the ones with cans and soft plastic, and write the section letter on the orange tag. We should not fill a bag so heavily that someone cannot lift it comfortably. I can bring the small luggage scale too, although its display was fading when I tested it on Tuesday. If it stops showing numbers, we can use the hanging scale only.

I will check the weather again at seven and text the group if there is a change to the meeting plan. Please give me your cell number if you are coming with someone whose name is not on the signup sheet, because the parks desk asked me for an approximate head count. I have the printed sheet, but it still has last year's phone numbers on the back, so I am making a fresh contact list tonight.

One last thing: the cleanup is meant to be relaxed, and nobody needs to stay for the full morning. If you need to leave early, tell me before you go so I can check that your bags or tools are not left along the path. We will gather by the rack at about eleven thirty, sort out the equipment, and take a quick group photo only if everyone is comfortable being in it. After that, the town truck is scheduled to collect the filled bags from the marked spot near the lot entrance, not from the beach.
